title: How to Break Down a Trade
hook: One case. Seven stages. The ending goes last.

launchpad.outcome: Follow Dayli through one full breakdown, in order, with the outcome hidden until the end.
launchpad.missionQuestion: What did I know before the trade?

slides.title: How to Break Down a Trade

case.title: How to Break Down a Trade

context.text: No scheduled news inside your window

marks.why: The top of the 4H dealing range: the highest point price has respected on this window.
The bottom of the 4H dealing range.
The 1H swing high price pulled back from. This is the level the session is building toward.
The 1H low that produced the shift.
The last lower high before the low. Closing above it shifted the 1H structure.
The 1H swing level price pulled back from, tested again in the session. Price has to close through it before anything else counts.
The first candle to CLOSE through the PIL. A wick through doesn’t count.
Price pulls back after the indication: the candle that closes back toward the PIL.
The candle that closes beyond the indication’s extreme. That close confirms the move.
After continuation, price comes back to the PIL and holds. This is the planned entry.

expert.decisionWhy: The full sequence formed in a room that supported it: thesis, PIL, I-C-C, retest, defined risk.

reasons.analysis: Bullish 4H room from the lower half, 1H shift, 15M correction into the level.
reasons.execution: Entered on the retest after a closed continuation.
reasons.risk: Stop beyond the correction low, 1 contract inside the plan.
reasons.management: Stop left where it was. No interference.

expert.lesson: Every stage was done in order. The stop getting hit doesn’t reach back and change any of them.
expert.management: Hold to target, stop stays where it is
expert.managementWhy: Your saved plan decides this, not the open P&L.

risk.why: Stop beyond the correction’s extreme (20369.75), target at 2.0R toward the 1H objective. Size comes from that distance and your risk profile, not from how good it looks.

The first candle to CLOSE through the PIL. A wick through doesn’t count.
Price pulls back after the indication: the candle that closes back toward the PIL.
The candle that closes beyond the indication’s extreme. That close confirms the move.
After continuation, price comes back to the PIL and holds. This is the planned entry.

reveal.headline: OUTCOME
reveal.note: Notice where you looked first just now. If your review starts with “I lost…”, you started at the wrong part of the trade.

steps.title: Welcome to the desk
lines: Seven phases of learning. Now you apply it. From here, every trade gets broken down the same way, in the same order.
4H room → 1H map → 15M observe → 1M execute → risk → management → outcome.
The outcome is locked. You’ll see it last, after the read is done. Watch me do this one, and follow along.

steps.title: 4H · READ THE ROOM

asks.q: What is the higher-timeframe structure saying?
asks.why: Dayli reads this room as bullish: price rejected the range low and is building higher lows on the 4H.

asks.q: Where is price inside the room?
asks.why: Price sits about 38% of the way up the 4H range.

prompts: Where is price inside the room?
demoLines: External high: the top of the room. Every 4H rally has stopped here.
External low: the floor. Price was defended here and rallied.
Price is coming off the floor and building higher lows. I’m reading the room as bullish, from the lower half.

steps.title: 1H · BUILD THE MAP

options: A bullish shift: price closed above the last lower high
A bearish shift: price closed below the last higher low
asks.why: The 1H closed above the last lower high (MSS), then pulled back. The swing it pulled back from is the level to watch.

prompts: Which level is the context for the PIL?
demoLines: The swing price just pulled back from. That’s the level the session will test.
The low that started the move.
The MSS: the last lower high, now closed above. The 1H map turned.

steps.title: 15M · OBSERVE

asks.q: What is the 15M doing into the session?
options: Correcting: pulling back after the 1H push
Sweeping: running a high or low and snapping back
asks.why: The 15M pulled back from the 1H level and is coming into the session from a higher low. That’s a correction, not a reversal.

demoLines: Nothing to mark here. The 15M is where I watch behavior.
Price pulled back from the 1H level and is coming into the open from a higher low. It’s correcting, not breaking.

pauses.text: Indication. A candle just closed through the PIL. A close, not a wick. Now I wait.
Correction. Price pulls back. I don’t chase the indication. This pullback is part of the model.
Continuation. This candle closed beyond the indication’s extreme. Confirmed.
Retest. Back to the PIL, holding. This is where my entry plan lives.

steps.title: Would you take it?
lines: I would. Everything I needed is there. Your turn: decide, and set the risk.

options: Hold to target, stop stays where it is

steps.title: Good trade?
steps.q: Before anything else happens: is this a good trade?

options.label: Yes, based on the process: every stage checks out
options.say: That’s the only thing you can judge right now. Good.

options.label: I can’t know until I see the outcome
options.say: You can. You can judge the process, and that’s all you could ever judge before the click.

options.label: It depends whether it hits the target
options.say: That’s judging by the ending. Look at what was true before it.

steps.text: IF YOUR REVIEW STARTS WITH “I LOST…” YOU STARTED AT THE WRONG PART OF THE TRADE.

lines: Here’s your read against mine. Toggle Decision view and Hindsight view above the chart. Drag Time-travel to see exactly what was known at each candle.

takeaways: Every review runs in the same order: 4H → 1H → 15M → 1M → risk → management → outcome.
The outcome is the last stage, not the first.
Judge the decision with what was known at the decision.
remember: If your review starts with “I lost…”, you started at the wrong part of the trade.
